fee_name: Sewer Impact Fee (per fixture unit)
formula_text: $401.17 x number of plumbing fixture units (toilet, lavatory, tub, shower, sink, dishwasher, washing machine, garbage disposal, urinal, bidet, sump pump or ejector = 1 unit each; floor drain, condensate drain, drinking fountain = 0.25; stub-outs = the fixtures they will serve)
source_title: Sewer Use Charge Ordinance for Rate Change October 1, 2025, Art. IV.E (fixture units Art. II.B)
notes: Levied 'upon each new connection to the System regardless of county jurisdiction'; the total depends on the home's fixture count. The ordinance has no residential minimum or flat residential rate; for non-domestic flow equivalence (Art. II.B.4) it defines a domestic household as 12 plumbing fixtures. Stub-outs are charged for the fixtures they will serve. Fixtures installed without payment can be billed double. Credits apply for existing connected fixtures (remodel/demolition, septic conversions up to 16 fixtures). Same $401.17 rate on the FY2026 Worksheet for Impact Fees (effective Oct 1, 2025). The calculator's unit count is the fixture count.

unit_label: deposit against actual cost, all sizes
source_title: Meter Charges and Miscellaneous Service Fees (Rev. October 2025)
notes: All sewer attachments, regardless of size, require a $2,000 deposit at application. Final charge is based on BGMU's actual time and materials to excavate, install pipe and appurtenances, backfill, restore, and any associated road cut/repair; overpayment refunded, shortfall invoiced. This is BGMU's standard sewer connection charge for a new home.

fee_name: Sewer Lateral Camera Fee
source_title: Meter Charges and Miscellaneous Service Fees (Rev. October 2025)
notes: Optional service to locate or check an existing customer sewer line using BGMU's camera; requires a cleanout on the property and freely-running sanitary sewer, requested 24 hours ahead. Not a new-construction connection charge.

fee_name: Sewer Tap Locate Fee
source_title: Meter Charges and Miscellaneous Service Fees (Rev. October 2025)
notes: Paid in the office before work; BGMU locates an existing sewer tap and installs a two-way cleanout at or near the property line. A separate optional service from the Sewer Attachment Fee that a brand-new connection pays. If a customer's own plumber installs the cleanout, camera use to locate the tap is $100 instead.

fee_name: Manhole Core Fee
source_title: Meter Charges and Miscellaneous Service Fees (Rev. October 2025)
notes: Charged when a new sewer connection requires coring an existing manhole rather than a standard lateral tap, regardless of size; paid before work. Contractor excavates and marks the manhole; BGMU cores it and installs the boot; contractor then connects the new sewer or lateral, and BGMU inspects. Not typical for a standard new single-family lateral.

fee_name: Application Fee - Water and/or Wastewater
source_title: Rules and Regulations, Section 3 (Application Fees), Approved November 2025
notes: Charged for each new water/wastewater account, collected at application; non-transferable and non-refundable. An account-opening charge, not a connection/tap charge, so it is kept out of the connection total (the same treatment as Kentucky American Water's $28 activation fee on the Lexington page). Electric service has a separate $35 application fee; after-hours applications are $60 per service.

fee_name: Water Meter Fee (1-inch)

fee_name: Water Meter Fee (4-inch) - Down Payment for Time and Material

fee_name: Water Meter Fee (5/8-inch)
source_title: Meter Charges and Miscellaneous Service Fees (Rev. October 2025)
notes: Smallest/standard meter size on BGMU's table. Flat fee for the meter itself, due at application. If BGMU must install a service line from the tap to the meter, that work is billed separately at time and materials, with no published flat rate.

notes: PRC fee covers engineering review for connecting to "the System" (water and sanitary sewer together, per the Fifth Amendment to the Water & Sanitary Sewer Service Agreements). Identical PRC and MCC schedules, at identical dollar amounts, are printed in both a water-fund cover memo (pp. W-35-W-37) and a nearly word-for-word sewer-fund cover memo (pp. S-34-S-35); both are titled "Integrated Connection Fees" and describe the charge as the cost of connecting to "the System" (singular). That paired-memo structure reads as the same combined fee being recorded in two fund ledgers for accounting purposes (one memo per utility fund), not as two separate customer-facing PRC charges -- which is also why the MCC explicitly needs the "only one MCC shall be charged" clarification: without it, a reader pulling the schedule from either memo alone could double-count a fee that is genuinely metered/purchased once. The source never states as explicitly for PRC that it is billed once, so this remains our reasoned reading rather than a directly quoted rule; we count it once (the conservative, lower total) and disclose the ambiguity on the page. 3/4" is Grand Rapids' smallest/standard meter size (no 5/8" tier is published).

notes: Minimum sewer PIF set by the Water and Sewer Board (Code Sec. 20-325); the city's 2025 tap fee sheet says it is charged by size of the domestic water tap, and single-family homes normally have a 3/4-inch tap. The 2026 Rate Manual computes residential-lot PIFs as a percentage of 'the applicable tap size-based values', a table that lists both water and sewer PIFs, but prints no sewer amounts by lot type; it is unclear whether the 50-70% shares also reduce the sewer PIF on lots under 6,000 sq ft. fee_name: Cash-in-Lieu of Raw Water Dedication
formula_text: lot acres x 3 acre-feet per acre x $57,000 per acre-foot
source_title: 2026 Rate Manual - Greeley Water & Sewer (Development; Cash-In-Lieu of Raw Water Dedication)
notes: Every new lot must satisfy Greeley's raw water requirement (3 acre-feet per acre of land for single-family, Code Sec. 20-255), either by dedicating accepted water rights at final plat, Terry Ranch credits, or this cash payment at building permit. Many subdivisions dedicate water at plat, so the cash amount is not owed on every lot. Price set by Water and Sewer Board motion; the March 2025 city sheet listed $56,500. Lower requirement possible with deed-restricted low-water landscaping. Code Sec. 20-257: a parcel over one-half acre with one detached home is instead set at 1.5 acre-feet (60,000 gallons if irrigated by a private non-potable system). Cash is due no later than building permit issuance (Sec. 20-254).

notes: Greeley Code Sec. 20-262 bases the single-family water PIF on residential lot type; the 2026 Rate Manual sets it as a percentage of the 3/4-inch tap value ($16,900) by lot size and irrigation source. Paid at building permit (Sec. 20-263/20-265). 100% of the printed 3/4-inch value. fee_name: Single-Phase Service Extension Installation Charge (embedded-cost credit)
formula_text: Estimated cost of the distribution facilities needed to extend service to the premises (excluding transformers), minus a $1,859 average depreciated embedded-cost credit for single-phase secondary-voltage service (includes residential and farm customers). If the estimated extension cost is at or under $1,859, the customer pays nothing; amounts above the credit are billed to the customer (in a new subdivision, the developer initially advances the cost and is refunded as connections are made, per Rule 201.2(g)).
source_title: Wisconsin Electric Power Company, Volume 17 -- Electric Rules and Regulations, Section 201.2(b) Installation Charges
notes: PSCW Docket 5-UR-111, order dated Dec 19, 2024, effective for service furnished on/after Jan 1, 2026. Statewide We Energies rule (not Milwaukee-specific), but it is the rule that governs a new single-family home in Milwaukee. Most infill single-family connections to an existing line fall under the $1,859 allowance and cost the homeowner nothing; long extensions (rural lots, not-yet-built-out subdivisions) can exceed it. We Energies will provide one free written cost estimate per 12-month period on request.

unit_label: per foot of frontage, capped at 200 feet
formula_text: Applicant's proportionate share = (applicant's frontage, up to 200 ft) / (total frontage served) x RWA's actual installation cost of the main -- no flat per-foot rate is published
source_title: Rules and Regulations for Water Service, January 2026 (revised May 18, 2026)
source_org: South Central Connecticut Regional Water Authority (RWA)
notes: Applies only where the property's water main was itself installed at RWA's expense or under an Advance Payment Extension Contract (Rules Section L.7-8) -- i.e., mainly new subdivisions/developments where RWA or a prior developer extended the main, not routine infill lots on long-existing New Haven streets with mains already in place. RWA does not publish a flat per-foot dollar rate; the charge is based on RWA's actual cost to install that specific main, apportioned by frontage (max 200 ft counted per service). No dollar figure can be computed without a specific main and frontage; confirm applicability and amount with RWA before budgeting. Minimum 10 feet of deeded frontage is required to receive service at all (Rules, Extension of Water Mains, Section II.18).

source_org: Sewerage & Water Board of New Orleans
notes: SWBNO does not publish a fixed dollar tap or connection fee. Under Act 227 (2020), amending La. R.S. 33:4090, SWBNO no longer provides free water/sewer connections to lots of record; the property owner hires a Louisiana-licensed Municipal & Public Works contractor (and a separately licensed master plumber for the private side) to build the connection to the public main. The contractor files a Service Cut Application with a plan drawing, construction cost estimate and schedule; SWBNO's House Connections Department (625 St. Joseph St., Suite 261) reviews it (about two weeks) and then charges an administrative fee equal to 20% of that estimate, covering inspections, technical review, documentation and meter preparation. Because the fee is a percentage of a private, lot-specific construction estimate, SWBNO does not publish -- and we could not find -- a single dollar figure that applies citywide. Same 20% figure repeated on the Connection FAQ page (https://www.swbno.org/Business/ConnectionFaq). The same 20% rate also applies to a new fire hydrant installation. Recorded as service=water (duplicated on the sewer side below) so the site's calculator surfaces the real SWBNO rule instead of falling back to a generic national tap-fee estimate -- it is still one 20% charge, not two.

fee_name: Water rights for Will-Serve Commitment (dedication or purchase, Rule 7)
formula_text: Acre-feet required = [1 / (1 + 19,000 / lot sq ft)], minimum 0.11 AF per lot, x 1.11 for mainstream Truckee River rights (x 1.00 for groundwater rights); rights are bought on the open market and dedicated, or a Will-Serve Commitment is bought from TMWA inventory at a price TMWA recalculates monthly
source_title: Rule 7 - Requirements for Will-Serve Commitment Letters (Section E amended 12/11/2025)
notes: No dollar amount is published: TMWA prices its Will-Serve inventory monthly from acquisition costs (Rule 7 G.3), and most developers buy rights privately. Example demand: 7,000 sq ft lot = 0.269 AF x 1.11 = 0.299 AF; 10,000 sq ft lot = 0.345 AF x 1.11 = 0.383 AF.
